figures.caption: Fig. 1. Workflow for the computational multiscale approach adopted in this research paper. The procedure starts with initial atomic structures used in first-principles calculations, DFT, and AIMD. The data generated from these calculations is used as a training set to develop a Deep Learning Potential for Machine Learning (ML) Molecular Dynamics. The ion transport parameters obtained from MD simulations are subsequently used to develop the continuum model. Finally, the results from both Machine Learning MD and the Continuum Model are analyzed to reach a coherent conclusion and provide recommendations. 2

Fig. 3. Schematic of the workflow for developing a Deep Learning Potential (DLP) for Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics (MLMD). Atomic coordinates obtained from AIMD data are used as inputs to neural networks that predict atomic energies and forces for MLMD simulations. The embedding neural network generates descriptors from atomic coordinates and passes them to the fitting neural networks. The fitting neural networks output the atomic energy contributions, which are summed to obtain the total energy and corresponding forces. thickness of the passivating interphase layer on the LGPS side esti­ mated by the 1D continuum model was used to calculate the charge- transfer resistance at the cathode|solid-electrolyte (LCO|LGPS) interface. Distribution of lithium inside the LCO cathode was assumed to follow a solid solution mechanism, where mass transfer occurs through a diffusion process model

Fig. 4. DFT vs DLP energies (a) and forces (b–f) for atoms at the LCO|LGPS interface, i.e., cobalt (Co), germanium (Ge), lithium (Li), oxygen (O), and phosphorus (P). FDFT and EDFT are forces and energy, respectively, calculated from DFT-generated data. FDLP and EDLP are predicted forces and energy, respectively, generated using the DLP. Fig. 5. Equilibrium plots of temperature (T, K), kinetic energy (KE, eV), potential energy (PE, eV/atom), and pressure (P, bar/atom) for the Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics simulation. The simulation of the (001)LGPS|(010)LCO interface was performed for ~3 ns using a Deep Learning Potential. The thermodynamic properties begin to stabilize at approximately 2 ns, indicating the system approaches equilibrium beyond this time. 6
